messages:
jess (Support): Hey team — ticket from a few customers hitting 401s in the Console and SDKs after they signed in via SSO. They report an immediate MFA prompt after authenticating and then it drops them back to sign-in. Repro steps included below.

kevin (Platform Eng): Can you paste the exact error the SDKs are returning? Is this just the Console or also server-to-server API keys?

jess (Support): Console + browser-based SDK flows only. Server API keys are unaffected. Error from the frontend: `401: session_invalid` and the Console shows a modal "We couldn't verify your session, please sign in again". Customer report: works on Firefox but Chrome 118+ fails consistently.

mira (Security): Noted — Chrome changed stricter SameSite enforcement recently. Do we set `SameSite` on the session cookie for the Console?

jess (Support): From the customer's HAR they attached: `Set-Cookie: rwd_session=eyJ...; Path=/; Domain=redwood.ai; HttpOnly; Secure; Max-Age=3600` — no SameSite attribute. They access the Console from `console.redwood.ai`.

kevin (Platform Eng): That Domain looks suspicious. It should probably be `.redwood.ai` (leading dot) or set on the exact host. Chrome sometimes blocks cookies without `SameSite=None; Secure` for cross-site contexts (iframe/postMessage/OAuth redirects). The SSO callback hits `auth.redwood.ai` which then redirects to `console.redwood.ai`. If cookie lacks `SameSite=None` it's treated as Lax and might not be sent on cross-site POST redirect.

sam_ops: I pulled auth logs for the timeframe: `2026-09-14T17:22:10Z auth-service ERROR session_lookup failed id=<redacted> reason=missing_cookie flag=invalid_session_cookie trace=tx-9f3a` — multiple traces with `invalid_session_cookie`.

kevin (Platform Eng): Good repro. Can someone grep for `invalid_session_cookie` across all auth pods? `kubectl logs -l app=auth -c auth | rg "invalid_session_cookie"` — I'll run a quick check in staging and prod.

oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-741 — elevated to P2 because multiple paid customers affected.

mira (Security): Also flag: we rotated our IdP certificate two days ago. Some SAML responses from a subset of customers' IdPs are returning `SubjectConfirmationData` with `NotOnOrAfter` very close to now (clock skew?). If the cookie is created but immediately rejected on return due to mis-timed assertion, that could cause a one-time drop too. But the Chrome correlation + missing SameSite strongly points to cookie handling.

jess (Support): Customer repro steps they sent: 1) Go to console.redwood.ai 2) Click SSO -> choose enterprise IdP 3) Complete SSO + MFA on IdP side 4) Redirect back -> Console shows temporary spinner -> then MFA modal again -> finally signs out. Provided a HAR and a video.

kevin (Platform Eng): Proposal: two immediate mitigations: 1) set `SameSite=None; Secure` on `rwd_session` cookie for auth.redwood.ai -> console.redwood.ai flows, 2) change Domain to `.redwood.ai` so subdomains get the cookie. Both are low-risk config changes. I'll open a quick rollbackable flagged deploy.

mira (Security): Before we push, confirm no CSP/third-party concerns. Also let's ensure the cookie is HttpOnly and encrypted (it is). Setting SameSite=None is fine. For IdP rotation: I'll re-check SAML certs and clock skew alerts.

kevin (Platform Eng): Creating patch: `auth-service: add SameSite=None to rwd_session cookie and set Domain=.redwood.ai` — will ship to canary first. Runbook: If we see increased `session_reject_count`, roll back.

sam_ops: Canaryed to 3% — monitoring set: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/metrics?m=session.invalidations per minute. Early telemetry shows success for canary users on Chrome.

jess (Support): I've replied to affected customers: temporary workaround - use Firefox or a private window, or we can force re-login after we flip the flag. They asked if they need to re-enroll MFA — no, should not need re-enroll, just re-auth.

kevin (Platform Eng): Patch merged to `main` with feature flag `auth.legacy_cookie_compat`. Rolling to 100% in 20m if no regressions. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/auth/pull/4829

mira (Security): Follow-up: I validated SAML cert rotation logs — some IdPs are returning assertions with 5s skew. I opened a ticket with Identity to request longer `NotOnOrAfter` tolerance on our side (20s grace window) and added a metric for `saml.clock_skew_violations`.

sam_ops: After full rollout, incidents dropped to baseline. Closing INC-2026-741 pending postmortem.

jess (Support): Filing a short postmortem and customer-facing note. Action items: (kevin) add unit test for cookie attrs, (mira) add SAML tolerance dashboard, (support) update KB article about browser cookie behavior and SSO.

kevin (Platform Eng): Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

mira (Security): Great catch, jess. :eyes:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-741 marked resolved at 2026-09-14T18:40:00Z
